reviewer: Implementing Codex agent; not blinded stakeholder review
observations: Reading estimate responds from 90-150 to 20-35 minutes; coffee from 45-75 to 15-30. These are model experience estimates, not measured durations.
Rainy context changes weather advice while preserving destinations; exact order need not change.
Cloudy-but-low-rain context is described distinctly; solar references remain unchanged.
The model explicitly identifies that sparse weather samples do not cover the morning solar window.
Deprioritizing photography changes light priority to not_relevant and uses no solar reference.
noncriticalIssues: Evening is translated as malam despite the supplied evening fixture being 17:00-18:00 local. This is a source-label/localization ambiguity that must be normalized before a product uses daypart advice; no numeric timestamp was rewritten or invented.
A6 uses curah tercatat for a zero-amount synthetic forecast field; the surrounding text explicitly calls it a synthetic forecast, but diprakirakan would avoid an observation implication.
Weather explanations can be repetitive; clear-scenario advice is more cautious than actionable.
The main-spot anchor remains the park in the low-photography case while reading/food are prioritized. The output respects the anchor but its prose has an experience-priority tension.
scope: Only the four pre-registered Phase B calls; no prompt repair, retries, UI, deployment or production acceptance.
